subject.title: fix(baseten): reject malformed model metadata numbers

question: Should Baseten live-model metadata accept a documented subset of numeric strings, or should OpenClaw accept JSON numbers only and treat all strings as unsupported provider input?
rationale: The upstream documentation inspected confirms the metadata surface but does not define a string-number grammar, so choosing the permanent compatibility boundary is a provider-policy decision rather than a mechanical parser repair.

options.title: Define and preserve a documented string grammar
options.body: Specify the accepted decimal forms from observed/provider-confirmed metadata, cover boundary cases, and retain fallback behavior for malformed values.

options.title: Accept JSON numbers only
options.body: Reject all string values after confirming Baseten does not emit them and document the stricter provider boundary.

recommendation.title: Define and preserve a documented string grammar
recommendation.body: Specify the accepted decimal forms from observed/provider-confirmed metadata, cover boundary cases, and retain fallback behavior for malformed values.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current parser and can supply the observed provider evidence, while current-main area ownership was not available from the read-only environment.
